cues.en: Mike: In this video, I'm going to tell you about a quantity that we derive from signal detection theory, it's called d-prime.
cues.zh: Mike：這支介紹從訊號偵測理論推導的 d-prime。

cues.en: Sometimes that's written out with the word-prime and sometimes it's abbreviated as D and then a single apostrophe, I'll show you that spelling later.
cues.zh: 有時完整寫 prime，有時寫 d 加單引號，稍後展示。

cues.en: D-prime is one of the most important and also one of the most commonly used metrics that we can derive from signal detection theory.
cues.zh: d′ 是從訊號偵測理論中，能推導出的最重要、也最常使用的指標之一。

cues.en: It's a really important metric because it allows us to quantify accurate performance.
cues.zh: 重要在能量化準確表現。

cues.en: So to motivate why we need something like d-prime I wanna get back to this experiment.
cues.zh: 為說明需要它的原因，回到實驗。

cues.en: So again, we have our lovely, kind, gentle, really helpful research participant and we put her in the room and we explain how the experiment works.
cues.zh: 親切、溫柔、熱心的參與者進房間，聽實驗說明。

cues.en: And she has to say whether she saw the light flicker or didn't see the light flicker and then we leave the room.
cues.zh: 回答有沒有看到閃光，之後我們離開。

cues.en: And then, after being in this experiment for an hour, we look at her behavioral data and we see what she's doing here and it turns out she has tons and tons of hits.
cues.zh: 一小時後，看行為資料，發現很多命中。

cues.en: Really, really a lot of hits and zero misses, not a single miss in the entire experiment.
cues.zh: 非常多，零漏失，整場一次都沒有。

cues.en: Now, at first, we look at her data and we think, man, she has amazing visual perception she has the best eyes ever but then, we start getting a little bit suspicious.
cues.zh: 起初以為視覺超好、眼力最好，但開始懷疑。

cues.en: Why doesn't she have a single miss?
cues.zh: 為何一次都沒漏？

cues.en: Why is her hit rate so high?
cues.zh: 命中率為何這麼高？

cues.en: So, we call her back in and we sit her down in a chair and say, "What's going on?"
cues.zh: 叫她回來坐下，問怎麼回事。

cues.en: And she says, "You know, I'm not as lovely and helpful and kind and gentle as you think I was actually being really mean and I was intentionally ruining your experiment.
cues.zh: 她說：「我沒你們以為的那麼好，其實很壞，故意破壞實驗。

cues.en: And the way that I did that was as soon as you left the room, I closed my eyes, I turned around so I wasn't even facing the computer screen.
cues.zh: 你們一離開，我就閉眼、轉身，不看螢幕。

cues.en: I put on headphones and started listening to a podcast and I was just pressing the yes key over and over and over again for an hour.
cues.zh: 戴耳機聽 Podcast，一小時一直按『是』。

cues.en: I was just pressing present as often as I could."
cues.zh: 盡可能按『有』。」

cues.en: Okay, maybe I got a little carried away there with my imagination.
cues.zh: 也許想像得有點過頭。

cues.en: But anyway, the point is, how can we distinguish whether someone has a lot of hits because they really saw the flicker because they were really doing the right thing
cues.zh: 重點是，如何區分命中多是因為真的看見、做對，

cues.en: or if they were not even paying attention to the experiment and just pressing yes all the time?
cues.zh: 還是根本不專心，只是不斷按是？

cues.en: How do we distinguish between those two possibilities?
cues.zh: 如何區分？

cues.en: That's a question for you.
cues.zh: 問你這個問題。

cues.en: If you would like to pause the video and think about how you would go about discriminating two situations like that, then please do so.
cues.zh: 想暫停思考如何區分，就請暫停。

cues.en: Okay, did you figure it out?
cues.zh: 想出來嗎？

cues.en: So the answer is that we can also look at the false alarm rate.
cues.zh: 也看誤報率。

cues.en: So the idea is that if she is just pressing yes all the time, she's constantly saying present, she's gonna have a lot of hits, but she's also gonna have a lot of false alarms.
cues.zh: 如果她一直按「是」，不斷回答「存在」，命中就會很多，但誤報也會很多。

cues.en: So the number of hits and the number of false alarms is gonna be both high and both equal in the way that she's doing this.
cues.zh: 這樣命中與誤報數都高、都相等。

cues.en: And furthermore, these two will be zero, but we'll get back to that in a later video.
cues.zh: 另外兩項是 0，後面再談。

cues.en: So this is the main idea, we compare the proportion of hits to the proportion of false alarms and that gives us a measure of perception of accuracy
cues.zh: 比較命中與誤報比例，取得知覺準確性指標，

cues.en: that actually reflects real accuracy and not just a bias towards saying yes all the time okay, and that is d-prime.
cues.zh: 反映真正準確性，而不只是一直說是的偏誤，這就是 d-prime。

cues.en: Here you see the two alternate spellings of d-prime.
cues.zh: 兩種寫法。

cues.en: So d-prime is a measure of discrimination this is not social political, economic discrimination, this is a measure of discrimination in the signal detection theory context,
cues.zh: d-prime 衡量辨識能力，不是社會、政治、經濟的歧視，而是訊號偵測的辨識，

cues.en: which basically just means you can separate this quadrant from this quadrant.
cues.zh: 基本上是能區分這個象限與那個象限。

cues.en: And we need d-prime because it's necessary to distinguish between all yes responses, which would be hits plus false alarms
cues.zh: 需要區分所有「是」，也就是命中加誤報，

cues.en: versus correct yes responses, which are only hits.
cues.zh: 以及正確的「是」，只有命中。

cues.en: So d-prime is therefore, a more accurate measure of performance compared to just looking at the number of hits.
cues.zh: 所以比只看命中數，更準確衡量表現。

cues.en: So pretty straightforward and it's a pretty simple derivation from signal detection theory.
cues.zh: 直接、簡單的推導。

cues.en: So here's how it works, there's a little algorithm to compute d-prime.
cues.zh: 計算有個小演算法。

cues.en: So what we do is we start by converting hits and false alarms into proportions relative to the total number of veridical events.
cues.zh: 先把命中與誤報，除以對應真實事件總數，轉成比例。

cues.en: So this is important, it's not the total number of events per se, but the total number of veridical events.
cues.zh: 不是全部事件總數，而是真實事件的對應總數。

cues.en: So it's the marginal total along the reality dimension, that was fun to say.
cues.zh: 沿現實維度的邊際總和，這句念起來很有趣。

cues.en: So it looks like this, so we say the probability of hits is the number of hits divided by the number of hits, plus the number of misses.
cues.zh: 命中機率，等於命中數除以命中加漏失數。

cues.en: So we need to divide hits by the marginal sum here of this column when reality was present.
cues.zh: 以現實中有訊號這一欄的邊際總和，作分母。

cues.en: Well, I guess reality is always present, but when the object was present in objective reality.
cues.zh: 現實當然總在，但指客觀現實中物件存在。

cues.en: Now, you might actually recognize this.
cues.zh: 你可能認得。

cues.en: This is just a conditional probability.
cues.zh: 就是條件機率。

cues.en: This is the probability of saying yes, given that the object was actually present.
cues.zh: 物件實際存在時，回答是的機率。

cues.en: So this is our probability of hits, and then we need to compute the probability of false alarms and that's basically the same computation.
cues.zh: 這是命中機率，接著誤報機率，算法基本相同。

cues.en: So it's the number of false alarms divided by the number of false alarms, plus the number of correct rejections.
cues.zh: 誤報數除以誤報加正確拒絕數。

cues.en: So again, it's the number of of things in this bucket, the number of items we have in here, plus the total number of reality absent trials in total.
cues.zh: 也就是這個格子的項目數，相對現實中沒有訊號的試次總數。

cues.en: Okay, then what we wanna do is take those proportions and convert them into a standard Zed score and there's a couple of reasons for doing this,
cues.zh: 接著把比例轉標準 Z 分數，有幾個原因，

cues.en: for converting the probabilities into standard Zed scores.
cues.zh: 為什麼把機率轉標準 Z。

cues.en: One of them is to stretch out the extremes a little bit.
cues.zh: 一個是拉開兩端。

cues.en: So we have higher sensitivity as we get towards extremely high proportions and extremely low proportions.
cues.zh: 比例很高或很低時，敏感度更高。

cues.en: You can see that by converting from probability to Z, we get a larger dynamic range here.
cues.zh: 機率轉 Z，動態範圍變大。

cues.en: So that kind of facilitates the interpretation.
cues.zh: 方便解讀。

cues.en: Furthermore, this is also useful for statistical reasons because we've converted a metric that is uniformly distributed
cues.zh: 統計上也有用，因為把均勻分布指標，

cues.en: to a metric that is normally distributed.
cues.zh: 轉成常態分布指標。

cues.en: So this facilitates subsequent analyses that rely on Gaussian distributions like regression, ANOVA, t-tests and so on.
cues.zh: 方便迴歸、ANOVA、t 檢定等依賴高斯分布的後續分析。

cues.en: Okay, so how exactly does this work?
cues.zh: 如何運作？

cues.en: Well, we look up the proportion of hits and false alarms on the Y-axis here, and then we draw a line over to where it meets the curve here,
cues.zh: 在 Y 軸找命中、誤報比例，畫線到曲線，

cues.en: this cumulative probability density, and then we draw a line down to the X-axis.
cues.zh: 累積機率密度，再往下到 X 軸。

cues.en: So this would be the probability of heads, and this would be the standard Zed score of that probability.
cues.zh: 這是命中機率，這是其標準 Z 分數。

cues.en: So here, for example, the probability of heads is 0.75, I guess, and the corresponding Zed score is actually, it's also kind of close to 0.75,
cues.zh: 例如命中機率大概 0.75，對應 Z 也有點接近 0.75，

cues.en: but I think you get the idea.
cues.zh: 你應該懂概念。

cues.en: For more extremes, You know, when you get a probability of hits being around 0.9, that would correspond to a Zed score of like a little over one, I guess.
cues.zh: 更極端，例如命中 0.9，Z 大概略高於 1。

cues.en: So this would be for the probability of hits and then here we have the probability of false alarms, that's a negative Zed value in this case, and then d-prime is a simple subtraction
cues.zh: 這是命中機率，這裡誤報機率，這例 Z 為負，再計算 d-prime，單純相減，

cues.en: of these Zed score differences.
cues.zh: 取兩個 Z 分數之差。

cues.en: So the d-prime in this example, using these numbers would be somewhere around 0.7 minus 1.3, so that's gonna be around two.
cues.zh: 這例約 0.7 減 1.3，所以大約 2。

cues.en: So the false alarm rate is generally negative and we're subtracting it.
cues.zh: 誤報的 Z 通常為負，減去它，

cues.en: So that's gonna make the d-prime be larger.
cues.zh: 讓 d-prime 更大。

cues.en: So you can see d-prime is not super complicated to derive or to compute.
cues.zh: 推導、計算不太複雜。

cues.en: And again, the idea is that it's more accurate or it's a better measure of accuracy because we are not only looking at the proportion of heads,
cues.zh: 更準確、是更好的準確性指標，因為不只看命中比例，

cues.en: but we are subtracting off, we're removing any bias that's introduced just by pressing yes all the time and having a lot of false alarms.
cues.zh: 也扣除一直按是、大量誤報帶來的偏誤。

cues.en: I would like to walk through an example with actual numbers, just to give you a feel, make sure you really internalize the algorithm for computing d-prime.
cues.zh: 用實際數字走一遍，確保真正理解演算法。

cues.en: So here's our data.
cues.zh: 這是資料。

cues.en: We have 22 hits, eight misses, three false alarms, and 27 correct rejections.
cues.zh: 22 命中、8 漏失、3 誤報、27 正確拒絕。

cues.en: That is our table of data.
cues.zh: 資料表如此。

cues.en: Now, I would like you to compute d-prime based on the algorithm that I showed in the previous few slides.
cues.zh: 請根據前幾張投影片，計算 d-prime。

cues.en: So please pause the video compute d-prime, and then when you have it come back and I will walk through the solution.
cues.zh: 暫停，算完回來，我會說明解答。

cues.en: Okay, so I hope you took that opportunity to do it.
cues.zh: 希望你把握機會。

cues.en: I mean now it's sort of towards the end of the course, but I hope you have been taking all these opportunities to pause the video and really engage with the learning material.
cues.zh: 雖然已到課程後段，希望一直都有暫停、積極投入學習。

cues.en: Alright, so let's see, here's our algorithm again.
cues.zh: 再看演算法。

cues.en: So we convert hits and false alarms to proportion.
cues.zh: 命中與誤報轉比例。

cues.en: So that gives us a proportion of hits of 0.73 and a proportion of false alarms of 0.1.
And then we have convert that into standard Zed scores, and I got 0.62 and minus 1.28, and then we just subtract those
cues.zh: 轉標準 Z，得到 0.62 與負 1.28，再相減，

cues.en: and that gives us a d-prime of 1.9.
cues.zh: 得到 d-prime 1.9。

cues.en: So I hope this is also the answer that you got.
cues.zh: 希望你也一樣。

cues.en: Of course, you know, I'm truncating these numbers here, so yeah, I mean it's possible you have some slightly, slightly different level of precision here, but it should be 1.90.
cues.zh: 數字截短，精度可能略有不同，但應是 1.90。

cues.en: Okay, so that's just a number, how do we interpret d-prime here?
cues.zh: 只是一個數字，怎麼解讀？

cues.en: Well, d-prime, it runs on a line and basically we can think of a d-prime of zero as being pure guessing.
cues.zh: d-prime 在數線上，0 基本上是純猜。

cues.en: A d-prime of one is generally considered to be pretty good and a d-prime of two is like totally red.
cues.zh: 1 一般認為不錯，2 則超棒。

cues.en: In theory, d-prime can get larger, but, you know, you're gonna get some false alarms generally.
cues.zh: 理論可更大，但通常還有些誤報。

cues.en: So usually a d-prime between one and two is considered to be quite good discrimination.
cues.zh: 一般 1 到 2，就算很好的辨識。

cues.en: Now, of course, a lot of this interpretation is relative, so you might want to be comparing d-prime across different individuals, across different groups
cues.zh: 當然解讀相對，可能比較不同個體、群組，

cues.en: of individuals or different conditions in an experiment.
cues.zh: 或實驗條件的 d-prime。

cues.en: Now, in theory, d-prime can be negative, that's mathematically possible.
cues.zh: 理論也能負，數學上可以。

cues.en: What would it mean?
cues.zh: 代表什麼？

cues.en: What are the circumstances where d-prime would actually be a negative number?
cues.zh: 何時會負？

cues.en: Yeah, so d-prime is gonna be negative when people have more false alarms than they have hits.
cues.zh: 誤報比命中多時。

cues.en: So if someone has more false alarms and fewer hits, then d-prime is gonna be negative.
cues.zh: 更多誤報、更少命中，d-prime 就負。

cues.en: And if that's actually happening, then either there's a mistake somewhere, maybe there's a mistake in your experiment, there's a mistake in your analysis code
cues.zh: 真發生，可能某處出錯，實驗或分析程式有錯，

cues.en: or, you know, whatever is caught is creating your data is doing something horribly wrong.
cues.zh: 或產生資料的東西做得很不對。

cues.en: So you shouldn't really ever see a d-prime that's negative, that generally indicates that something went wrong somewhere, but it is possible to get a d-prime of around zero.
cues.zh: 不太應看到負 d-prime，通常表示某處錯，但接近 0 可以。

cues.en: One word of caution. d-prime actually doesn't work when the hits or false alarms are exactly 0% or exactly 100%.
cues.zh: 提醒，命中或誤報恰為 0% 或 100%，d-prime 無法運作。

cues.en: Then I'm not going to tell you why right now, but I would like you to figure out why.
cues.zh: 不直接說原因，請自己想。

cues.en: And if you need a little bit of a hint for understanding why this would be the case, you can go back to the slide where I showed the cumulative probability distribution,
cues.zh: 如果需要一點提示，來理解為什麼會這樣，可以回到我展示累積機率分布的投影片，

cues.en: mapping the probabilities onto the cumulative distribution and see if you can figure out the answer there.
cues.zh: 看看機率如何對應累積分布，想出答案。

cues.en: Okay, the last point I wanna make here is that d-prime is insensitive to response bias.
cues.zh: 最後，d-prime 不受反應偏誤影響。

cues.en: So what does that mean?
cues.zh: 什麼意思？

cues.en: What is response bias and what does it mean for d-prime to be insensitive to response bias?
cues.zh: 反應偏誤是什麼，不敏感代表什麼？

cues.en: That's a great question and you have to keep watching to find out the answer.
cues.zh: 好問題，繼續看才知道。

cues.en: So in this video I introduce you to d-prime, as I mentioned in the beginning, I'm pretty sure this is the most commonly used metric of signal detection theory.
cues.zh: 這支介紹 d-prime，前面說過，相信是訊號偵測最常用指標。

cues.en: It's really important, it's a great measure of accuracy because it separates accurate responses from just saying yes all the time.
cues.zh: 很重要，能區分準確反應與只是不斷說是，是很好的準確性指標。
